paragraphs.text: # dsh-dev-workflow
中文 | English
A conventions gate for DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
check the commit message before it commits · the PR description before it opens · the version before
it releases · ask before a command that cannot be undone · 200–250 tokens resident
dsh plugin --profile web add @melosic/dsh-dev-workflow
If your `git commit`, `gh pr create` and `git tag` are run by an agent, these checks are for you. Th
e rest of this file covers only when it speaks up, and why.
## Why
Every project writes some conventions down — how a commit message is shaped, which sections a PR car
ries, how a version is chosen. They usually live in `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and a document or
how a version is chosen. They usually live in `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and a document or two.
Text does not enforce itself. Reading a rule and following it are two different things: the guide sa
ys the subject stays under 50 characters and the agent still writes 62. This plugin turns the parts
a machine can check into checks that run — at commit, pull request and release time — and stops to a
sk before anything irreversible.
What it saves is rework:
release discovered to disagree with `package.json`.
It only touches three kinds of action: the ones awkward to change once committed, seen by others onc
e pushed, and gone once run.
Two words recur below:
- **Triggers** check the work against the project's rules at commit, pull request and release time.
- **Guards** stop before a command or a file operation runs.
## When it speaks
| You are | It does |
| `git commit` | Checks the message format, whether a `feat` added a CHANGELOG entry, and whether do

cs moved with the code |
| `gh pr create` | Checks the description for the sections the template ask

s for, unticked checklist items, and a linked issue |
| `git tag` / `npm publish` | Checks the versi

on is semver, that tag and `package.json` agree, and that the changelog has the section |
| `git res

et --hard`, `rm -rf`, `git push --force` | Stops and asks first |
| Reading `.env`, a real secret in
the arguments | Refuses — no per-call approval |
The rest of the time it says nothing.
What it says when it stops you is one line of why, plus the safer alternative:

> **A force push rewrites remote history and can discard other people's commits.**
> Prefer `--force
-with-lease`: it refuses to overwrite commits you have not seen.
## How it works
The plugin hangs off DSH's tool-execution chain. Before the agent runs a command or writes a file, i
ngs off DSH's tool-execution chain. Before the agent runs a command or writes a file, it looks once:
One layer judges "is this within the rules" — commit messages, PR descriptions, version numbers. The
other judges "can this be undone" — lost work, rewritten history, things others will see. When both
fire, there is one prompt showing both sets of reasons, never two questions in a row.
The full spec is not on this path either: it stays resident as one summary line and is read only whe
n needed, which is why the resident cost is 200–250 tokens.
## The five guards
| Guard | Blocks | Default |

| Command | `rm -rf /`, `mkfs`, `dd of=/dev/sda` — irreversible | ask |
| git | `reset --hard`, `cle

an -f`, `push --force`, branch deletion, `--no-verify`, `git restore .` | ask |
| Outward | `push`,

`tag`, `gh pr create`, `gh issue create`, `npm publish` — others will see it | ask |
| Sensitive fil

es | `.env`, `*.pem`, private keys, the `credentials` file and directory | deny |
| Credentials | A
real secret in the command arguments | deny, unless the line only reads |
The first three ask rather than refuse: most of these actions are legitimate, they are just worth on
e confirmation. The last two refuse — reading a private key has no "fine once you confirm it" case,
and printing the path in an approval dialog is itself a second leak, so there is no per-call approva
l. The false positives are already excluded: sample files such as `.env.example` do not count, and n
either does `grep -rn "credentials" .` — the check that tells you whether a secret is in the tree, b
ecause a search expression is not a path. To make one file readable, drop it from `fileGuard.noRead`
or turn that guard off.
The credential guard has one exception, and it is a judgement rather than a setting: a command line
whose every program only reads — `grep`, `rg`, `sed -n 's/…/…/p'`, `git log -S` — is let through and
recorded as a hit. The value is already in the argument the model just wrote, so refusing the searc
h removes nothing and stops nothing; it only hides the leak from whoever is looking for it. One prog
ram on the line that could write or send puts the refusal back. The judgement is about what the line
will actually run, not what it is named: `sed -i` writes the file back, `sed -f` reads a script tha
t is not on the line, the `e` flag (`s/a/b/e`) runs the replacement, and `$(…)` / `<(…)` can hold a
second program inside what looks like one word. None of those counts as reading.
In a session with approvals turned off, "ask" becomes a refusal, and the prompt says how to get past
session with approvals turned off, "ask" becomes a refusal, and the prompt says how to get past it.
## Requirements
| Component | Version | Notes |

| DeepSeek Harness runtime | `0.2.0-rc.2` or `0.2.1-rc.2` | `dsh --version` |
| Node.js | `>=20` | r

equired by dsh itself |
| pnpm | any; not checked | only needed by `dsh plugin`, and it must be on `

by dsh itself |
| pnpm | any; not checked | only needed by `dsh plugin`, and it must be on `PATH` |
Those are the only two versions, not a range: they are the ones this plugin has actually been loaded
on, and a range would also claim every 0.2 prerelease in between and every 0.3 after them. The cost
is that a new DSH prerelease needs a new release of this plugin — which is the honest direction, be
cause "not tested" should read as "unsupported". When the version is one of the others, **`dsh plugi
n add` refuses the install outright** (`dsh: installation rejected: Plugin … is incompatible with ds
h …`, nothing is installed) and prints the `dsh plugin allow-version` escape hatch. An already-insta
lled older copy behaves differently: the plugin is disabled at startup with `dsh: disabling profile
plugin …` on stderr, and the rest of the profile loads normally. Both say why; neither is silent. Ch
eck `dsh --version` against the list above before filing a bug, and paste the output of `/dev-workfl
ow status` into the issue; how the list is chosen is in docs/PUBLISHING.md.
